name: Nodular Neuronal Heterotopia

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Radiological and Clinical Diagnostic Criteria for Neuronal Heterotopia

criteria.description: Identification of nodular clusters of neurons in abnormal locations on brain MRI
Presence of focal or generalized seizures consistent with neuronal migration disorder
Histological evidence of ectopic neuronal clusters in brain tissue (if biopsy performed)
Cognitive or developmental delay associated with neuronal migration abnormalities

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: MRI evidence of nodular neuronal clusters plus clinical seizures consistent with neuronal heterotopia
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Histopathology is rarely performed but confirms diagnosis; genetic testing may support but is not diagnostic.

imaging: MRI showing nodular clusters of grey matter in subcortical white matter
FLAIR and T1-weighted sequences highlighting heterotopic nodules
genetic: Mutations in FLNA gene (in some familial cases)
Other neuronal migration disorder-associated gene variants

distinguishingFeatures: Location of nodules adjacent to lateral ventricles
Presence of continuous band of grey matter beneath cortex
Often associated with DCX gene mutations

redFlags: New onset focal seizures in childhood or adolescence
references: Barkovich AJ et al. Classification system for malformations of cortical development. Neurology. 2012.
Guerrini R, Dobyns WB. Malformations of cortical development: clinical features and genetic causes. Lancet Neurol. 2014.
Orphanet Report on Nodular Neuronal Heterotopia, ORPHA:2149
